description: What PROD actually did for each named package slice, read-only, used as the comparison baseline for the DEV canary and the full-window DEV run, and how each slice's real PROD-derived inputs are built. Each slice names one baseline source. A slice with baselineKind none falls back to schema, row-count and reject-reason checks, and the report says so. Silvally never builds a local oracle in place of a missing actual.

source.meaning: Interprose's own SMS log rows, mirrored read-only by Stage ETL
source.freshness: the table's maximum _stage_output_timestamp must reach the window end (a re-committed snapshot is not enough); otherwise the slice uses the most recent UTC day its data covers and the stale mirror is a data-platform handoff

key.rationale: sms_log emits only provider QUIQ status edges (sms_log.sql: provider = 'QUIQ'), with vendor_tracking_code = provider_tracking_code, plus debt_id, phone_number, msg, sent_date, vendor_result, txt_msg_template_id, te_id and interaction_identifier. txt_msg_log mixes every SMS vendor: on 2026-09-04..06 every row that carried vendor_tracking_code had txt_msg_vendor_id 67 (3/3, 16/16, 1/1) and no txt_msg_vendor_id 34 row carried one, so the 2.5% population of the whole table is the legacy vendor's rows, which sms_log never produces. The comparison population is therefore txt_msg_vendor_id 67 (rowFilter.actual), keyed by vendor_tracking_code; a row without a tracking code (for example an opt-in or opt-out status) is keyed by the always-populated composite debt_id, phone_number, sent_date. compare reports keyCoverage, so a wrong vendor id or an unpopulated key fails visibly instead of silently.

dayCounts.rationale: sms_log.sql emits a row only for a status edge with provider = 'QUIQ', so an input day counts only when it has such edges; graph_inputs.py edge-days counts them per UTC day

daySelection.rule: the most recent complete UTC day with BOTH txt_msg_vendor_id 67 rows in the mirror AND provider QUIQ status edges in PROD Persist, within a 14-day lookback counted back from the lookback anchor: today, or, when the mirror is stale, the day its data cutoff (dataMax of _stage_output_timestamp) falls on, so the mirror's most recent covered day stays reachable; the anchor moves back at most 30 days
daySelection.actualDays: iceberg_snapshot_read.py --table interprose_current.txt_msg_log --window-column sent_date --start <today - 44 days> --end-exclusive <today> --where txt_msg_vendor_id=67 --data-max-column _stage_output_timestamp (byUtcDay; one read bounded to the 14-day lookback plus the 30-day maximum anchor shift)
daySelection.inputDays: graph_inputs.py edge-days --slice sms --lookback-days 14 --end-day <anchor - 1 day> (per-day count of provider QUIQ edge-text-message-status-changed edges over the same anchored lookback; the anchor is the dataMax day when stale, else today)
daySelection.choose: source_window.py data-days --most-recent --lookback-days 14 --slice-days <actual days> --input-days <input days> --data-through sms=<dataMax> --catalog reference/prod-actuals.json (records each slice's lookback anchor)
daySelection.noDay: BLOCKED: the slice reports UpstreamInputEmpty (and ProdMirrorStale when the mirror stops first) plus this entry's blockedHandoffs

sensitiveFields.decision: ownerDecisions.sensitiveFieldStaging = stage-real-values-to-dev: the real values are staged to DEV unmodified and compared directly. Without it the slice stops with SensitiveStagingDecisionRequired (ask the owner).

prodTransformRuns.checked: 2026-09-30, read-only: every execution of the PROD Transform state machine (us-east-2 TransformPipelineStack-transform-pipeline, 141 executions from 2026-09-21) and every run plan under its data bucket's runs/ (149 plans)
prodTransformRuns.finding: PROD Transform has executed only interprose-to-graph@1.0.0; no lexicon-to-interprose version, and so no sms_log output, has ever run in PROD. A PROD Transform run cannot stand in as the SMS actual; the Interprose mirror is the only actual.
prodTransformRuns.recheck: list runs/<execution>/plan.json in the PROD Transform data bucket and match mapping.id lexicon-to-interprose with sms_log among the outputs

blockedHandoffs.detail: interprose_current.txt_msg_log data ends 2026-09-06 although the table is re-committed; refresh the mirror so a day after the Persist SMS status edges begin is covered

PROD Persist edge-text-message-status-changed edges start 2026-09-13 and carry provider null; sms_log.sql keeps only provider = 'QUIQ', so no day has both a mirror row and an emitted sms_log row. Populate provider QUIQ on the status edges (or change the carried query's filter, a mapping CONFIGURATION decision)
hydration of edge-text-message-has-rendered-artifact-uri found objects whose SHA-256 differs from the edge's content_sha256; fix the artifact or the recorded digest so message bodies can be verified

knownRisks.detail: the carried sms_log query filters provider = 'QUIQ' while current PROD status edges have provider null: on today's PROD graph the query emits no rows, and an unchanged query cannot prove it covers real SMS traffic until provider is populated

source.meaning: Interprose's debt settlement agency rows; an active row (empty delete_date) is the DSA_NAME Interprose actually holds for that debt
source.freshness: the table's maximum _stage_output_timestamp must reach the window end (a re-committed snapshot is not enough)

comparison.detail: form_1281 emits each debt's current DSA_NAME, so the window only selects debts: read the actual by key (prod_actuals.py keys, then iceberg_snapshot_read.py --key-column debt_id --keys-file) for the canary or window debts and compare the active row per debt. A debt with only deleted rows must produce no DEV row.

keyRead.selectKeys: iceberg_snapshot_read.py --table interprose_current.debt_settlement_agency --window-column last_update --start <day> --end-exclusive <day + 1> --data-max-column _stage_output_timestamp, then prod_actuals.py canary-sample (canary) or the whole window's rows, then prod_actuals.py keys --field debt_id: the window selects the debts
keyRead.readState: iceberg_snapshot_read.py --table interprose_current.debt_settlement_agency --key-column debt_id --keys-file keys.txt --current-state-as-of <dataMax of the selection read> --data-max-column _stage_output_timestamp (no --window-column): every row of each selected debt whose _stage_output_timestamp is at or before the mirror's data cutoff, not only the window's rows, so a DSA set before the window or deleted after it counts
keyRead.asOf: the mirror's data cutoff (prod_actuals.py table-summary dataThrough); the graph inputs use the same cutoff (graph_inputs.py --as-of)

graphInputs.asOf: when the actual's dataThrough precedes the graph's current state, build with --as-of <dataThrough> so edges created after the mirror stopped do not show as mismatches

source.stateMachine: DocumentProcessingStateMachine (EXPRESS; upload steps SliceUploadToInterprose and UploadToInterproseQC invoke lambdaFunctionName directly)
source.meaning: EXPRESS executions have no execution history API; their logging level ALL with includeExecutionData records every LambdaFunctionScheduled input and LambdaFunctionSucceeded or LambdaFunctionFailed result. A succeeded output is the registration Interprose accepted; a failure is an expected reject
source.inputField: LambdaFunctionScheduled details.input: the upload step Parameters, which is also the DEV classification_event input row
source.daySelection: prod_actuals.py probe-days (newest-first, bounded pages per day), then lambda-outcomes for the chosen day only

m2d.debtBinding: a debt-resolved event is compared against the debtID the PROD Lambda logged, not one Silvally derives
